La frattura a toro (buckle) è la frattur: The torus (buckle) fracture is the most common wrist fracture in children: the porous, elastic metaphyseal bone buckles under compression instead of breaking. The sign is a small bulge or an abrupt angulation of the cortical contour, often on one side only and in only one view (here the lateral, dorsal side). It is found by following the cortical contour from the diaphysis to the physis: it should be a smooth curve. It is stable and heals well with a splint; the differential diagnosis is with greenstick fracture (opposite cortex interrupted) and with complete fracture.
Segui il profilo della corticale metafis: Follow the contour of the metaphyseal cortex in both views: any bump or abrupt angle in a child is a torus fracture until proven otherwise.
